# Parity Studio

Parity Studio turns a screenshot or sketch into a componentized `ui_kit/` — real .tsx components
and tokens.css — and judges the result against a 16-check deterministic parity rubric. The score is
reported honestly on every iteration, including when it drops. It also works as a design-staging
layer for an existing codebase: capture the current UI, decompose it into editable slugs, prove
what changed, apply only the approved deltas.

## Canonical links

- [Parity Studio](https://parity-studio.vercel.app/)
- [Source code](https://github.com/HomenShum/parity-studio)

## NodeSlide moved

NodeSlide, the deck-as-code editor, used to be served from this deployment at `?domain=nodeslide`.
It is now a separate product with its own repository and deployment.

- [NodeSlide](https://nodeslide.vercel.app/)
- [NodeSlide source](https://github.com/HomenShum/NodeSlide)

Old `?domain=nodeslide` and `?share=<id>` links on this host redirect there, and will keep doing so
until at least 2026-10-25. Do not cite this host as a source for NodeSlide behavior.

## Product behavior

- Parity checks are deterministic and named; the passing count is never rounded up or floored.
- Decomposition emits editable component files, not a flattened image.
- A comment scopes to a selected file and a pinned bounding box, so an iteration rewrites a slice
  rather than the whole artifact.
- Model tier, timing, token and cost telemetry is exposed per run rather than summarized away.
- External model access requires an explicit key and consent.

## Agent access

Use the in-product Keys and BYOK surface for connection instructions and scoped tools. Exported
`ui_kit/` bundles are user-authored artifacts; verify their contents rather than assuming parity.
